blocks.heading: Questions Before You Commit to This Path

items.text: A single salary figure, or one relative's opinion about "marine engineers earning well," cannot tell you whether this path genuinely fits your specific situation.
Can you genuinely sustain 4-on, 8-off watchkeeping rotations in a hot, loud engine room for 5-8 month stretches, with broken sleep and limited personal space, without it wearing you down.
The engine department's physical demands are different from the deck side: heat, noise, and machinery-space confinement are a daily reality, not an occasional inconvenience.
Marine engineering does not have to mean sailing for an entire career.
Marine surveying, if you enjoy inspection, documentation, and technical judgment more than hands-on repair

Marine surveyors inspect vessel machinery, hull condition, and cargo systems on behalf of owners, charterers, or insurers, and typically require several years of sea service before a surveying qualification is even open to you.

blocks.heading: Avoid When Deciding on Marine Engineering

items.text: A DG Shipping approval number and a verifiable list of companies that actually hired last year's graduating batch matter far more than campus photos or a placement percentage claimed in a brochure.
Legitimate agents are paid by shipping companies for placing qualified officers, not by candidates for a promised job.

visuals.heading: 4th to Chief Engineer

figures.label: Estimated Time Required
figures.source: After accumulating the required sea time as a watchkeeping officer (commonly totalling 24-30 months across 4th and 3rd Engineer ranks), the officer sits the MEO Class II exams, a substantially harder written and oral test covering machinery operation, maintenance planning, and engine-room management.

figures.label: Estimated Time Required
figures.source: After further sea time as 2nd Engineer, usually another 24-36 months depending on vessel type and company policy, the officer sits the MEO Class I exams, the top-level Certificate of Competency covering full technical, legal, and managerial responsibility for the ship's machinery.

visuals.heading: Not a Flat Yes or No

items.text: You are genuinely comfortable with, and have discussed with family, the reality of repeated 5-8 month sea contracts with engine-room watchkeeping shifts.
You have a real interest in mechanical, thermal, and electrical systems specifically, not just the general idea of a seagoing career.
You are prioritising strong, tax-advantaged early-career income and are willing to trade lifestyle flexibility and years of exam preparation for it.

You have a realistic plan to clear MEO Class IV, II, and I on schedule, plus, eventually, a deliberate plan for a shore-based technical role rather than an open-ended assumption about sailing indefinitely.
